shortTitle: 4.13 Termination of Resuscitation & Verification of Death

guide.title: Termination of Resuscitation & Verification of Death
guide.lead: Knowing when not to start, and when to stop, is part of good resuscitation. Follow clear rules with medical direction, think of the special cases, and care for the family as much as the patient.

sections.title: Don't start
include: Blunt trauma: pulseless, apneic, no organised rhythm on arrival
A valid DNR, POLST or advance directive
exclude: Any doubt: start and seek advice
Hypothermia, drowning, pregnancy, children, suspected poisoning: resuscitate

sections.title: Termination rules (with medical direction)
notes: EtCO₂ below 10 mmHg after 20 minutes of ALS is one factor, never the only one.

steps.title: Tell the family
steps.text: Sit down, use their name and say "died", not euphemisms.

steps.title: Support
steps.text: Answer questions; call family, friends or a faith leader.

steps.title: Record
steps.text: Time of death and the decision process.

steps.title: Scene
steps.text: Possible crime: touch as little as possible; notify police or the coroner per local rules.

items.label: Asystole
items.sub: Confirm in 2 leads and check the gain

quiz.q: Which finding allows you to withhold resuscitation?
Before terminating resuscitation in the field you generally must:
The family shows a valid DNR during an arrest. You should:
options: Honor it and give comfort care
Not witnessed by EMS, no shock delivered, no ROSC
quiz.explanation: The ALS rule adds no bystander witness and no bystander CPR.

quiz.q: EtCO₂ below 10 mmHg after 20 minutes of ALS:
options: Is one factor in the decision, never the only one
quiz.explanation: Combine it with the whole picture.

quiz.q: Blunt trauma, pulseless, apneic, no organised rhythm on arrival:
options: Resuscitation can be withheld per protocol

quiz.q: Best words when telling a family:
A death may involve a crime. You should:
options: Disturb the scene as little as possible and notify police
Move the body to the ambulance
quiz.explanation: Document anything you had to move.

quiz.q: Which is NOT a reason to withhold resuscitation?

flashcards.question: Signs of obvious death
flashcards.answer: Decapitation, decomposition, incineration, rigor mortis, dependent lividity, injuries incompatible with life.
flashcards.category: Termination of Resuscitation & Verification of Death

flashcards.question: Dependent lividity
flashcards.answer: Blood pooling in the lowest parts of the body after death: reddish-purple discoloration.
flashcards.category: Termination of Resuscitation & Verification of Death

flashcards.question: Documents that withhold resuscitation
flashcards.answer: A valid DNR, POLST or advance directive.
flashcards.category: Termination of Resuscitation & Verification of Death

flashcards.question: BLS termination rule
flashcards.answer: Not witnessed by EMS, no shock delivered, no ROSC: consider termination with medical direction.
flashcards.category: Termination of Resuscitation & Verification of Death

flashcards.question: Telling the family
flashcards.answer: Clearly and kindly, using "died" or "dead", not euphemisms.
flashcards.category: Termination of Resuscitation & Verification of Death

flashcards.question: Possible crime scene
flashcards.answer: Disturb as little as possible, document what you moved, notify police.
flashcards.category: Termination of Resuscitation & Verification of Death

flashcards.question: ALS termination rule adds
flashcards.answer: Not witnessed by a bystander and no bystander CPR.
flashcards.category: Termination of Resuscitation & Verification of Death

flashcards.question: Special cases: keep going
flashcards.answer: Hypothermia, drowning, pregnancy, children, suspected poisoning.
flashcards.category: Termination of Resuscitation & Verification of Death

critical.scenario: A pulseless, apneic patient is cold, with obvious rigor mortis and dependent lividity.
critical.question: Appropriate action?

options.t: Withhold resuscitation, follow the death-in-the-field protocol and support the family
Call for ALS and start CPR

critical.kpi: Recognizes obvious death and withholds futile resuscitation

critical.scenario: An arrest not witnessed by anyone. After full CPR there's been no ROSC and every AED analysis said "no shock".
critical.question: Next step?

options.t: Contact medical direction to consider termination per protocol
options.f: Correct: the BLS rule is met.
Transport with CPR rarely changes the outcome here.

critical.explanation: Not witnessed by EMS, no shock, no ROSC.
critical.kpi: Applies BLS termination criteria with medical direction

critical.scenario: As you prepare to resuscitate a pulseless relative, the family produces a valid DNR/POLST.
critical.question: What do you do?

options.t: Honor it, withhold resuscitation, support the family and document
Resuscitate anyway in case they change their mind
options.f: A valid order must be honored.

options.t: Ask the neighbours what to do
Transport with CPR to let the hospital decide

critical.explanation: If the document's validity is unclear, start and contact medical direction.
